/-!
# Six standard deviations suffice (Spencer's theorem)

Spencer's theorem in discrepancy theory: for every $n$ and every family of $n$ subsets
$S_1, \dots, S_n$ of $\{1, \dots, n\}$, there is a colouring
$\chi : \{1, \dots, n\} \to \{-1, +1\}$ such that
$$\left|\sum_{j \in S_i} \chi(j)\right| \le 6\sqrt{n}$$
for every $i$.

A uniformly random colouring only achieves the bound $O(\sqrt{n \log n})$, so Spencer's
theorem ("six standard deviations suffice") is a genuine improvement over the basic
probabilistic method; its proof uses a partial-colouring argument based on the entropy
method, and the bound $\Theta(\sqrt{n})$ is tight up to the value of the constant.
Spencer's original argument is non-constructive; polynomial-time algorithms achieving
$O(\sqrt{n})$ were later found by Bansal (2010) and Lovett–Meka (2012).

The Komlós conjecture (the subject of a companion file in this directory) would
strengthen this theorem: applied to the incidence vectors of the sets, scaled by
$1/\sqrt{n}$, it would give a discrepancy bound $O(\sqrt{n})$ for any number of sets,
not just $n$ of them.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrepancy_of_hypergraphs#General_hypergraphs)
- [J. Spencer, *Six standard deviations suffice*,
  Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. **289** (1985), 679–706](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-1985-0784009-0)
- [N. Bansal, *Constructive algorithms for discrepancy minimization*,
  FOCS 2010, 3–10](https://doi.org/10.1109/FOCS.2010.7)
- [S. Lovett and R. Meka, *Constructive discrepancy minimization by walking on the edges*,
  SIAM J. Comput. **44** (2015), 1573–1582](https://doi.org/10.1137/130929400)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace SixStandardDeviations

/--
**Six standard deviations suffice** (Spencer, 1985)

For every $n$ and every family of $n$ subsets $S_1, \dots, S_n$ of $\{1, \dots, n\}$,
there is a colouring $\chi : \{1, \dots, n\} \to \{-1, +1\}$ such that
$\left|\sum_{j \in S_i} \chi(j)\right| \le 6\sqrt{n}$ for every $i$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem six_standard_deviations :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Fin n → Finset (Fin n)),
      ∃ χ : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ j, χ j = 1 ∨ χ j = -1) ∧
        ∀ i, |∑ j ∈ S i, χ j| ≤ 6 * Real.sqrt n := by
  sorry

/--
**The random colouring bound**

There is a constant $K > 0$ such that for every $n$ and every family of $n$ subsets
$S_1, \dots, S_n$ of $\{1, \dots, n\}$, there is a colouring
$\chi : \{1, \dots, n\} \to \{-1, +1\}$ with
$\left|\sum_{j \in S_i} \chi(j)\right| \le K \sqrt{n \log(n + 2)}$ for every $i$.
This follows from a Chernoff bound applied to a uniformly random colouring, and is
the benchmark that Spencer's theorem improves upon by removing the logarithmic
factor. (The shift $n + 2$ inside the logarithm is a harmless normalization keeping
it positive for $n \in \{0, 1\}$.)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/Lemmy00/spencer-random-coloring-lean/blob/a691214a7263c1010fdd10560091e9f8cfce903a/SpencerRandomColoring/RandomBound.lean#L37"]
theorem six_standard_deviations.variants.random_bound :
    ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Fin n → Finset (Fin n)),
      ∃ χ : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ j, χ j = 1 ∨ χ j = -1) ∧
        ∀ i, |∑ j ∈ S i, χ j| ≤ K * Real.sqrt (n * Real.log (n + 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check: with no points and no sets ($n = 0$), the empty colouring works and
the bound $6\sqrt{0} = 0$ holds vacuously.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem six_standard_deviations.variants.zero_sets (S : Fin 0 → Finset (Fin 0)) :
    ∃ χ : Fin 0 → ℝ, (∀ j, χ j = 1 ∨ χ j = -1) ∧
      ∀ i, |∑ j ∈ S i, χ j| ≤ 6 * Real.sqrt 0 :=
  ⟨Fin.elim0, fun j => j.elim0, fun i => i.elim0⟩

end SixStandardDeviations

findings.description:
The module docstring (lines 36-39) says the Komlós conjecture, "applied to the incidence vectors of the sets, scaled by 1/√n, ... would give a discrepancy bound O(√n) for any number of sets, not just n of them." Taken literally this is false. With m sets on n points the discrepancy is not O(√n) in general. The complete hypergraph (all 2^n subsets of an n-set) has discrepancy ⌈n/2⌉. For m ≥ n sets the correct bound is Θ(√(n log(2m/n))).

The remark swaps sets and points. Komlós signs the vectors it is given, so to colour the points it must be applied to the vectors indexed by the points: the columns of the incidence matrix, v_p = (1[p ∈ S_i])_i ∈ ℝ^n. These have norm ≤ √n when there are n sets. Scaled by 1/√n, Komlós then gives O(√n) for n sets on ANY NUMBER OF POINTS. Applying it to the sets' incidence vectors, as the docstring says, signs the sets rather than colouring the points, which bounds the transposed system. Also, 'n sets on any number of points with O(√n)' already follows from Spencer's theorem by the standard linear-algebra reduction, so in this respect it is not a strengthening. No Lean statement in the file is affected.
findings.source_evidence:
Cited Wikipedia page, 'Discrepancy of hypergraphs', Examples section: "The other extreme is marked by the complete hypergraph (V, 2^V). In this case the discrepancy is ⌈|V|/2⌉." (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrepancy_of_hypergraphs).

Y. Zhao, Probabilistic Methods in Combinatorics notes, Thm 5.1.3: "Let F be a collection of n subsets of [n] ... at most 6√n ... if F be a collection of m ≥ n subsets of [n], then we can replace 6√n by O(√(n log(2m/n)))". After Conj. 5.1.5 (Komlós): "Spencer's theorem implies the special case of Komlós conjecture where all vectors v_i have the form n^{-1/2}(±1,...,±1) ... The deduction is easy when m ≤ n. When m > n, we use [Lemma 5.1.6]". Here the m vectors are the points and n is the dimension, i.e. the number of sets.

Lovett–Meka (arXiv:1203.5747), Thm 1.1: disc < K√(n·log₂(m/n)) for n points and m sets.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the remark with, for example: "The Komlós conjecture (see `KomlosConjecture.lean`) generalizes this theorem. Applied to the columns of the incidence matrix (for each point $p$ the vector $(1[p \in S_i])_i \in \mathbb{R}^n$), scaled by $1/\sqrt{n}$, it gives discrepancy $O(\sqrt{n})$ for $n$ sets on any number of points." Optionally add that for $m \ge n$ sets on $n$ points the correct bound is $O(\sqrt{n \log(2m/n)})$.

reformulations.difference: The source gives the random-colouring bound as disc ≤ √(2n ln(2m)) (Wikipedia), i.e. O(√(n log n)) for m = n. The Lean states it as ∃ K > 0 such that for every n, every family of n subsets of Fin n has a ±1 colouring with every |χ(S_i)| ≤ K·√(n·log(n+2)): an explicit constant, the shift n+2, and only the case m = n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 1, 2n ≤ (n+2)², so √(2n ln(2n)) ≤ 2√(n ln(n+2)). The source's bound therefore implies the Lean with K = 2, and n = 0 is trivial. Conversely, the Lean is exactly 'disc = O(√(n log n)) for n sets on n points': for n ≥ 2, log n ≤ log(n+2) ≤ 2 log n. The finitely many small n are absorbed into K because log(n+2) > 0. The shift is needed, since at n = 1 we have log 1 = 0 while a singleton set has discrepancy 1. The docstring explains the shift. The Lean statement itself is formally proved by the linked external proof, which I compiled.

review.notes:
1. Constant 6 for all n. `six_standard_deviations` asserts ≤ 6√n for every n. The cited Wikipedia section says "In the case m=n, disc(H) ≤ 6√n can be shown for n large enough." I could not read Spencer's Theorem 1 verbatim: AMS and Wayback serve a Cloudflare challenge, and the PDF looks like a scan without a text layer. Every precise restatement I could read gives 6√n for every system of n sets on n points, with no threshold: the Lovett–Meka abstract and Thm 1.1 ('K can be 6 if m=n'), Bansal §1.1, and Zhao's Thm 5.1.3 (which follows Alon–Spencer). For n ≤ 36 the claim is trivial (|χ(S)| ≤ n ≤ 6√n); I proved this in a scratch file, and checked that 37 > 6√37, so the claim has real content from n = 37. I therefore judge the statement faithful. If a maintainer can read the scan, Theorem 1 of Spencer (1985) is the one place to confirm.

2. Wikipedia's 'General hypergraphs' item 2 ('m ≥ n ⇒ disc ∈ O(√n)') is itself missing the log(2m/n) factor. This is probably where the docstring's Komlós remark comes from (reported above as a minor finding).

3. The `formal_proof` record on `random_bound` checks out. The external repository pins Lean v4.33.1 and the same Mathlib revision as this checkout (0df444a…). I concatenated its five files into a scratch file and compiled it. `example : type_of% @SixStandardDeviations.six_standard_deviations.variants.random_bound := <external theorem>` elaborates, and `#print axioms` gives only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. No sorry, admit or native_decide.

4. Minor and not reported: `random_bound` is textbook-level (Alon–Spencer's basic Chernoff bound) but tagged `research solved`. The module docstring speaks of the Komlós conjecture in the conditional, while the companion `KomlosConjecture.lean` records it as solved (Sept 2026). Neither affects any statement.

Status: all three categories match the sources (Spencer 1985 solved; random bound solved and formally proved; test proved in the file). No status issues.
